meanings.note: Understanding or surprise. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'ah', common in natural conversation.
je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived
Qu'est-ce qui arrive?. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to arrive'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'arrivé').

examples.text: Non, je viens d'arriver. Mon père, mais c'est compliqué.
examples.trans: No, I've just arrived. My dad, but it's complicated.

meanings.note: No preposition: attendre quelqu'un. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.
Il vous attend?. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.

examples.text: Attendez-moi deux minutes devant le bureau!

examples.text: Nous attendons un appel très important de Los Angeles.
examples.trans: We are waiting for a very important call from Los Angeles.

meanings.note: As a warning shout: attention!. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'attention; careful!'.
Faire attention = to be careful. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'attention; careful!'.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!
examples.trans: Careful, you're heading for the road!
